ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Each of the twenty dots on the graph below represents one of Sarah's classmates. Classmates who are friends are connected with a line segment. For her birthday party, Sarah is inviting only the following: all of her friends and all of those classmates who are friends with at least one of her friends. How many classmates will not be invited to Sarah's party?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the center of the figure is an oval labeled "Sarah". Around it there are a total of 20 black dots representing classmates, and line segments indicate friendship relationships. In the upper left there is a small triangle made of 3 dots and line segments, which is not connected to the part where Sarah is located; on the left there is also a single isolated dot. Around Sarah there are several dots directly connected to the oval, and on the right and below there is also an outer chain-like connection. Reasoning: According to the graph distance marking method, first mark all dots directly connected to the Sarah oval; these are Sarah's friends. Then starting from these already marked friends, mark the one-step neighbors connected to them; these are friends of Sarah's friends. After completing the two-step marking, the unmarked dots include: the 3-dot triangle in the upper left that is not connected to Sarah, the 1 isolated dot on the left, and the 2 dots on the right/right-lower outer chain whose distance from Sarah is more than two edges. Therefore the number of classmates not invited is 3+1+2=6.

method.method_draft: Use a graph-distance marking method. From the image, treat the oval labeled Sarah as the starting vertex and each dot as a classmate. First mark every dot with a line segment directly touching Sarah; these are Sarah's friends. Next, for each marked friend, mark every dot connected to that friend by one line segment; these are friends of Sarah's friends. After this two-step marking, count the unmarked classmate dots. In the image, the unmarked dots are the 3-dot triangle in the upper left that has no connection to Sarah's component, the isolated single dot on the left, and the two dots on the far right/bottom-right outer chain that are more than two edges away from Sarah. Thus 6 classmates are not invited.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中中央是标有“Sarah”的椭圆，周围共有20个黑点代表同学，线段表示朋友关系。左上方有一个由3个点和线段组成的小三角形，它没有连接到Sarah所在的部分；左侧还有一个单独的孤立点。Sarah周围有若干直接连到椭圆的点，右侧和下方还有一条外侧链状连接。
推理：按图距离标记法，先标记所有与Sarah椭圆直接相连的点，这些是Sarah的朋友。再从这些已标记朋友出发，标记与他们相连的一步邻居，这些是Sarah朋友的朋友。完成两步标记后，未被标记的点包括：左上方不与Sarah连通的3点三角形、左侧的1个孤立点、以及右侧/右下外侧链上距离Sarah超过两条边的2个点。因此未被邀请的同学数为3+1+2=6。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the natural breadth-first search / distance-from-Sarah route: classify classmates by whether their graph distance from Sarah is 1 or 2, then count those at distance greater than 2 or disconnected.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph structure: the central Sarah oval, the 20 classmate dots, and which dots are joined by line segments. Identify the dots directly adjacent to Sarah, then the dots adjacent to those friends, and finally the unmarked dots.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the statement that Sarah invites all her friends and everyone who is friends with at least one of her friends, and that there are 20 dots representing classmates.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Bridge the party rule to graph theory: invited classmates are exactly the vertices at graph distance 1 or 2 from Sarah; not invited vertices are those at distance greater than 2 from Sarah or disconnected from Sarah.
